content: In tier 1 the compounds showed their parts.
Sun + shine, home + work: you could see how
they were made. Here the parts have fused.
Nobody hears onset as on + set. Used enough,
a word stops being built and starts being meant.
onset       on + set, a setting on
offspring   off + spring, what springs off
hallmark    hall + mark, Goldsmiths' Hall
earmark     ear + mark, on a beast's ear
Read the sum and the seam shows again: a
turncoat turned his coat inside out, a pitfall
is a fall into a pit. The French twins are
the formal ones: onset beside commencement,
downfall beside ruin, turncoat beside traitor.
THE NEXT 25 CARDS: seams that have healed.
UN- is two Old English prefixes that fell
together. One is not: untold, unrest, unsung.
The other undoes an act: to unleash is to
take the leash off. WITH- is Old English
with, against or back: to withstand is to
stand against, to withdraw is to draw back.
undo        un + do
unleash     un + leash
withstand   with + stand, against
withhold    with + hold, back
Some plain halves are dead: kempt, couth,
ruly, wieldy. Only the un- form lives on. The
French twins: undo beside reverse, uncover
beside reveal, withstand beside resist.
THE NEXT 33 CARDS: un- and with-.
The body is the first store of metaphor. Set
a head, a heart or a hand beside a plain word
and it names a character: the headstrong are
strong in the head, the heavyhearted carry a
heavy heart, the openhanded give freely.
headstrong  head + strong
heartfelt   heart + felt
handsome    hand + some, easy to handle
hamstring   ham + string, the tendon cut
Handsome once meant handy, easy to handle,
and only later good to look at. A skinflint
would skin a flint for its worth. The French
twins: handsome beside attractive, brainchild
beside invention, nosedive beside plummet.
THE NEXT 21 CARDS: head, heart, hand.
The weather and the ground gave English a set
of compounds that now mean something else. A
windfall was fruit blown down by the wind,
free for the taking; now it is any luck. The
bedrock was the rock beneath the soil.
windfall    wind + fall, fruit blown down
quicksand   quick, living + sand
lodestone   lode, a way + stone
groundwork  ground + work, the base
Quick meant alive, so quicksand is sand that
moves. The lodestone was the leading stone,
the one that showed the way. The French twins:
bedrock beside foundation, hailstorm beside
tempest, thunderstruck beside astonished.
THE NEXT 22 CARDS: wind, stone, fire, water.
A verb and a direction, set solid, make a
noun for what happened to you: a setback is
what set you back, a letdown is what let you
down, the fallout is what fell out after.
The parts are plain; the whole is a thought.
aftermath   after + math, a mowing
setback     set + back
upshot      up + shot, the last shot
hindsight   hind, behind + sight
The aftermath was the grass that grows after
the mowing; the upshot was the last shot of a
match. The French twins are the words of the
report: aftermath beside consequence, setback
beside obstacle, letdown beside disappointment.
THE NEXT 24 CARDS: nouns of thought.
UP- is Old English up, upward. On a verb it
lifts: to uphold is to hold up, to uproot is
to pull the roots up, to upend is to set a
thing on its end. On a noun it names a
rising: an uprising, an upturn, an upswing.
uphold      up + hold
uproot      up + root
uprising    up + rising
upkeep      up + keep, keeping it up
Some are newer than they look: update and
upgrade carry the up of up to date and up a
grade. The French twins: uphold beside
sustain, uprising beside insurrection,
upkeep beside maintenance.
THE NEXT 23 CARDS: up- words.
A verb and its object, set solid, name the
one who does it: a killjoy kills joy, a
scarecrow scares crows, a daredevil dares
the devil, a dreadnought dreads nothing. The
oldest of them have hidden their verb.
onslaught   on + slaught, a slaying
farewell    fare, to travel + well
wedlock     wed + lock, a pledge
scapegoat   scape, escape + goat
Wedlock has no lock in it: the lock was a
pledge, the pledge of the wedding. Farewell
is an order, travel well. The French twins:
onslaught beside assault, farewell beside
adieu, wedlock beside matrimony.
THE NEXT 20 CARDS: deeds set solid.
